# V2.0.0 - 🧱 The "Ground-Up" Update

## 🧰 Package Manager Status:
- Winget: ⏳ Not updated yet
- Scoop: ⏳ Not updated yet
- Choco: ⏳ Not updated yet

## ⬇️ Downloading the App
**The main downloads are `Setup-x64.msi`, `Setup-arm64.msi`, `Portable-x64.zip` and `Portable-arm64.zip`**
The rest is for the auto update functionality and **_does not_** need to be downloaded in order for the app to work.

## ⚠️ Coming From V1.9.0? Update From Inside the App
- **Use the built-in updater** (the update prompt, or Settings > About > Check for Updates). Your settings, saved scripts and history come along.
- **Do not run the new Setup over 1.9.0** (that includes `winget upgrade` and `choco upgrade`) without a backup: the *old* installer uninstalls itself first and, for most installations, deletes your settings and scripts before 2.0.0 ever starts. If you update that way anyway, export your settings and copy the `Scripts` folder from `%LOCALAPPDATA%\FluentTaskScheduler` first.
- This is the last time. From 2.0.0 on, every way of updating keeps your files.

## 🚀 New Features
- **Rebuilt From the Ground Up**: The 3,800-line main page is gone. All logic now lives in a Core library with about 1,800 unit and integration tests, and UI tests drive the real app on Windows x64 and ARM64 for every change. The app runs on .NET 10 and Windows App SDK 2.7. (#25)
- **Import Tasks From Anywhere**: Importing a task XML now opens a dialog that shows what the task runs and when, and lets you pick its name, folder, account (you, SYSTEM, or the one from the file) and privileges before anything is registered. Files exported on another PC or for another user just work. (#30)
- **A Task List That Keeps Up**: Tasks created in Windows' own Task Scheduler show up, and while Windows records task history the list follows what other programs create, change or delete, without a refresh. (#29)
- **Your Data, Your Call**: Settings, scripts, history and logs moved to `%LOCALAPPDATA%\TRGamer-tech\FluentTaskScheduler`, outside the installer's folder. Uninstalling and updating leave them alone. Want them gone? Settings > Data > **Delete App Data** resumes snoozed tasks, switches Start with Windows off, closes the app and deletes its files.
- **Fits Any Window**: The navigation pane folds to icons and then to a menu button as the window gets narrower, and the task editor, the task details and the settings give way instead of being cut off. (#27)
- **Runs Keep Running**: A script in the editor or a quick action that is still running carries on when you change the language or another setting that rebuilds the pages. The output stays too.
- **A Tray Icon You Can Read**: The running-task count is drawn for the size the notification area shows it at, at any display scaling, and the icon comes back after Explorer restarts.
- **Proper WinUI 3 Look**: Standard controls, styles and theme resources throughout, including the high contrast themes, and a welcome tour whose buttons stay put. (#24, #26)
- **Friendlier to Screen Readers**: Controls that were only "button" or "combo box" have names now, pages have headings, and a screen reader is told how a quick action ended or what the next tour slide says. Every page and dialog is checked against the rules of Accessibility Insights on each change.

## 🛠️ Fixes & Improvements
- **Triggers Finally Behave**: The trigger editor was rewritten. A trigger keeps the type, time, days and time zone you set, for daily, weekly and monthly triggers alike. (#21)
- **Saving No Longer Resets Your Task**: Saving starts from the task as Task Scheduler has it and changes only what you changed. The run time limit, the account, privileges and every setting the editor does not show stay as they were. (#28)
- **Snooze Done Right**: A snooze follows its task when the task or its folder is renamed or moved, a snooze until a picked time follows a change of time zone, and the app says honestly why a run was held back.
- **Dashboard You Can Trust**: No figures from half-read data, hours written the way your clock writes them, and it rests while the window is hidden.
- **Console Output in One Piece**: The output of sfc, DISM and other console programs arrives in full and in the right encoding.
- **No More Phantom Next Runs**: A disabled task no longer shows a next run it is not going to have.
- **Start With Windows Sticks**: It survives a reinstallation and an upgrade by a newer Setup.
- **Translations**: Every Japanese and Chinese text was reviewed again and now uses Windows' own terms; German says "du" throughout; 263 texts that nothing showed are gone.
- **Updates**: An update you put off is offered again instead of being installed behind your back at the next start.
- **Releases You Can Verify**: Each release is installed, uninstalled and reached from an installed 1.9.0 on a fresh machine before it is published, and the SHA-256 table below is written by the release workflow from the very files attached here. (#31)

## 🐛 Known Issues
- Running the 2.0.0 Setup over 1.9.0 resets the settings of most 1.9.0 installations (see above). Updating from inside the app does not.
- Tasks that are snoozed when you uninstall the app stay disabled. Resume them first, or enable them in Windows' Task Scheduler.
- Starting a task by hand from the app ignores the task's "Queue" and "Stop the existing instance" rules: Windows applies those only when a trigger starts the task.
- On Windows 10, install the current Windows updates first. On a long outdated Windows 10 the app may not start.
- Please report any feedback or bugs via GitHub Issues.
